title: SMTP notifications cannot use implicit-TLS servers (port 465) — EnableSsl only does STARTTLS
existing_state: SmtpDispatcher is built on System.Net.Mail.SmtpClient with EnableSsl = profile.UseStartTls (Services/Notifications/SmtpDispatcher.cs:86-90). SmtpClient's EnableSsl implements only STARTTLS upgrade on a plaintext connection; it cannot speak SMTPS/implicit TLS, so any relay that requires port 465 (common for hardened enterprise relays and most consumer providers' legacy submission ports) fails with an opaque handshake/timeout error in NotificationResult. SmtpClient is also formally deprecated by Microsoft with MailKit as the recommended replacement. The Settings UI offers only a 'UseStartTls' checkbox and a port spinner defaulting to 587 (SettingsDialog.cs:1314), with no security-mode choice and nothing warning the user that 465 won't work.
recommendation: Replace SmtpDispatcher's transport with MailKit's SmtpClient (single NuGet package, no native deps), mapping a new profile enum SmtpSecurity { None, StartTls, ImplicitTls } onto MailKit's SecureSocketOptions; keep UseStartTls deserialization as a back-compat alias mapping to StartTls. Expose the mode as a dropdown in the Notifications tab next to the port field (auto-suggest 587 for STARTTLS, 465 for implicit). The dispatcher is already virtual and isolated behind NotificationService, so the swap is contained to one file plus the model/UI fields.
user_benefit: Email notifications work against the full range of corporate and cloud mail relays, not just STARTTLS-on-587 ones — and the failure mode for the wrong port becomes a clear configuration choice instead of a cryptic timeout.
